_why: ADR 0109's table. The CLI now shows the papers the fallback search found,
and no longer claims PubMed returned nothing when it did not.
_why_two_files: THREE files, and the third was added because the harness demanded it.
The first set ran only the two CLI files and reported C1 and C3 NOT
CAUGHT. Both mutate `literatureResolver.ts` -- and the CLI tests MOCK
`resolveKinetic`, so the parsing this change actually fixed never ran.
The tests proved the command renders papers it is handed and proved
nothing about whether anything hands them over.
That is ADR 0027 verbatim: a test that pins a component tells you
nothing about the wiring. The bug lived in the first half of the pipe
and the tests covered the second.
`offlineResolverEndToEnd.test.ts` drives the real subprocess through a
stub runner -- the seam that exists for exactly this -- so the boundary
is exercised rather than mocked past.

mutations.description: a candidate with no locator is rendered anyway
_note: `parseCandidatePapers` drops entries with no title and entries with
no pmid, doi or url. A title with no locator is an unverifiable
claim, and the count printed to the student comes from the filtered
list so it can never promise more papers than it names.
Dropping the filter makes the count and the list disagree.
